items.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998
items.q: And Charlie Ventura came through, a great jazz saxophone player, Billy Butterfield came through, phenomenal, and I got to play with these people and learn from them.

ctx.x: Is there a series of jazz musicians, ensembles or engagements that you really think back fondly of?

I had an opportunity once, there used to be a jazz club in Hartford, Tobacco Valley, and they had a summer series. And at one point I became the house drummer. And Charlie Ventura came through, a great jazz saxophone player, Billy Butterfield came through, phenomenal, and I got to play with these people and learn from them. And they were of course apprehensive coming into what they would call a local area, using a local rhythm

section, but they were happy, most of the time they were happy. So I look back fondly on that. And certainly playing with some of the big bands, I performed with the Artie Shaw Band and Dick Johnson, another master. And each time I play with these people there’s something that I learn. The learning process is continuing, it’s wonderful.
